title: Human-in-the-loop trigger map and sample-weighting lab (WIP)
content:
Quick summary:
This is a working lab for mapping triggers that route requests to human-in-the-loop (HITL) review during staged LLM feature rollouts. Focus is on pragmatic sample-weighting heuristics (how we pick which requests get human review), a minimal operational rota, and telemetry signals that let operators scale HITL up/down without thundering the review queue.

Goals:
- Define a small, actionable trigger map for initial multiwave exposures (0.1% -> 1% -> 5%).
- Produce lightweight sample-weighting rules so early reviewers see high-signal examples.
- Specify telemetry and runbook actions for common pressure/failure modes.
- Keep ops overhead low: one primary reviewer on duty + an escalation path.

Non-goals:
- This is not the canonical ML evaluation suite. Do not try to capture every failure mode here.
- We are not designing long-term QA tooling (e.g., annotation platform workflows) — this covers on-call, short-term review.

Context and constraints:
- Target features: model reranking + structured extraction for user profiles. High downstream impact if hallucinations occur.
- Early waves: feature behind experiment flag, traffic slices limited by user cohorts.
- Reviewers are product QA engineers and solutions engineers with 30–60 min review SLA initially.
- Human reviews should be batched (10–50 samples) to preserve reviewer context but also must surface edge cases quickly.

Trigger map (ordered by priority for routing to HITL):
1) Safety heuristics match (immediate): any response that trips the safety blacklist (PII leak, legal advise tag) -> immediate routing.
2) High-confidence extraction mismatch (model vs cached truth): extraction confidence < 0.6 and conflicting with recent user-provided data -> HITL.
3) High business-impact paths: requests tagged as billing/change-account -> weighted sampling 100x baseline.
4) Novel tokens / hallucination proxy: out-of-vocab ratio > threshold OR generation contains domains not in allowed-domain list -> weighted sampling.
5) Low-latency-failure fallback: if model falls back to cheaper variant and difference score > delta -> sample 10%
6) Random baseline: uniformly sample 0.01% of all traffic as control set for drift monitoring.

Sample-weighting heuristics (practical rules):
- Base sampling weight = 1. Apply multipliers: safety-hit x1000, business-path x100, confidence-gap x50, novelty-proxy x20, fallback-delta x10.
- Cap final weight per-request to avoid one-off storms (max weight 5000 for a single request).
- Normalize: convert weights to probabilities using softmax-like capped mapping: p = min(0.05, weight / (weight + 1000)). This keeps extreme cases visible but bounded.
- Ensure temporal smoothing: if a user triggers >5 HITL samples in 1 hour, reduce their weight by 90% to avoid reviewer bias from single-user churn.

Batching and queueing rules:
- Batch size target: 25 samples per batch. Commit to dispatching at least one batch per 10 minutes when queue non-empty.
- Priority queue: safety hits > business-path > novelty > confidence-gap > baseline. Review UI should show priority badges.
- Max queue backlog before auto-fallback: 1,000 pending items -> stop routing non-safety items to HITL; route to automated fallback with verbose logging.

Reviewer workflow (SLA & steps):
- Primary reviewer (on-call) checks rotation channel every 10 minutes. Triage timeframe: acknowledge batch within 10m, finish batch within 60m for priority batches, 4h for low-priority batches.
- Steps: open batch -> verify label(s) -> annotate free-text note -> mark action: approve / modify / escalate. Escalation goes to lead reviewer or on-call eng team.
- If action = modify, system records delta and triggers automated patch (where supported) or a ticket in JIRA for product dev.

Telemetry & signals to monitor (minimal set):
- HITL-queue-depth: pending count. Alert at 250 (warning) and 1000 (critical).
- HITL-latency: median and 95th time from route->acknowledge. Alert if median > 15m.
- Safety-hit-rate: per-minute rate. If >5x baseline for 5m -> page safety lead.
- Human-override-rate: fraction of HITL items where human changes model output. Track weekly trend. If >10% sustained -> consider model rollback.
- Escalation-frequency: number of escalations to engineering per day. If >10/day for 3 days -> open incident review.
- Downtime/backpressure: percent of requests auto-fallbacked due to queue overflow.

Runbook actions (quick play):
- On HITL-queue-depth warning: notify rota via Slack, temporarily increase sampling cap for safety hits only, and spin up modal review session (30 min) for reviewers.
- On HITL-queue-depth critical: stop non-safety sampling, enable degraded mode for affected cohort, set traffic slice to fallback model, and open incident channel.
- On Human-override-rate spike: pause rollout for next exposure wave, require additional automated tests, and schedule a root-cause sync.

Rollout gating thresholds (suggested):
- Wave progression: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20%
- Progress each wave after 72h stable: no safety hits that require rollback, human-override-rate < 5%, no sustained latency or cost regressions (>20% token cost increase).

Pre-activation checklist (must pass to open HITL routing):
- Experiment flag toggles validated in staging and smoke tests pass.
- Safety rule set and blacklist reviewed with security.
- Initial sample-weighting config deployed to feature flagging system.
- On-call rota published and reviewer training doc shared.
- Dashboard created with queued signals + drilldowns for sample examples.

Post-activation monitoring cadence:
- First 2 hours: 5m sampling of telemetry, primary reviewer watches live feed.
- 2–72 hours: 15m rolling windows, daily sync with product and SRE.
- >72 hours: revert to baseline monitoring cadence (1h/4h) unless anomalies persist.

Edge cases and open questions (to resolve):
- How to surface contextual history without leaking sensitive user data to reviewers? (possible solution: tokenized/redacted context view — need privacy review).
- Should reviewers get an interface to annotate severity tags that feed back to model training pipelines? (yes, but out of scope for initial waves).
- Fine-tuning the novelty proxy: we need to benchmark false positive rate vs signal for several token thresholds. Action: Marco to run sampling job (JIRA-PLT-987).
- Reviewer fatigue: how to rotate without increasing latency? Consider rotating 1-week stints with daily micro-breaks.

Notes-to-self / informal ops tips:
- Keep a watchlist of high-value users to exclude from random sampling (internal accounts, founders) to avoid noise.
- For early waves, surface counterfactuals: show model baseline vs candidate side-by-side in UI. Rapidly helps reviewers calibrate.
- Add a tiny feedback form inside review UI: did this sample help you find a bug? Binary yes/no — track to measure signal value.

Action items / next steps:
- Marco: run novelty-proxy baseline job and attach sample set (due 2025-11-12).
- Dana: draft reviewer training doc and screenshots of review UI (due 2025-11-17).
- Zoe: wire telemetry dashboards (HITL-queue, human-override-rate) in Grafana and create alert policies (due 2025-11-24).
- Aisha (owner): schedule a dry-run with 2 QA reviewers and simulated traffic next week; capture latency and queue behavior.

Appendix: quick example rules (examples to seed the config file):
- rule: safety_blacklist -> weight: 10000 -> immediate: true
- rule: business_path[billing] -> multiplier: 100 -> cap: 5000
- rule: novelty_proxy[tld_unknown] -> multiplier: 20 -> cooldown: 10m

References and links:
- JIRA-PLT-987 (sampling job)
- CONFLUENCE-1234 (safety rule definitions)
- github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-templates/pull/52 (sample-weighting prototype)

This is intentionally light and operational — meant to be iterated quickly. Comments and edits welcome (please ping @aisha.p in Slack).
